BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]] | years4 = 2021–2022 | team4 = [[Pallacanestro Trieste|Trieste]] | years5 = 2022–2023 | team5 = [[ratiopharm Ulm]] | years6 = 2023 | team6 = [[Samsunspor Basketbol|Samsunspor]] | years7 = 2024–2025 | team7 = [[BC Körmend|Körmend]] | years8 = 2026–present | team8 = [[Zastal Zielona Góra]] | highlights = * Third-team All-[[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] (2018) * Big 12 All-Defensive Team (2018) | medaltemplates = {{MedalSport|Men's basketball}} {{MedalCountry|{{bk|MLI}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Africa Under-18 Championship]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[2014 FIBA Africa Under-18 Championship|2014 Madagascar]]|}} }} '''Sagaba Konate''' (born March 19, 1997) is a Malian professional [[basketball]] player playing as a center for [[Zastal Zielona Góra]] of the [[Polish Basketball League]]. He played college basketball for the [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia Mountaineers]]. A native of [[Bamako]], he moved to the United States to play at [[Kennedy Catholic High School (Hermitage, Pennsylvania)|Kennedy Catholic High School]] starting in his junior season. As a sophomore at West Virginia, he was named third-team All-Big 12 and made the conference All-Defensive Team.{{cite web|last1=Hertzel|first1=Bob|title=Carter named Big 12's top defender, joins Konate on all-defensive team|url=https://www.wvnews.com/sports/wvu/carter-named-big-s-top-defender-joins-konate-on-all/article_a0fb930f-3a70-5815-ad9d-d1455eb32ff4.html|publisher=WV News|accessdate=March 23, 2018|date=March 5, 2018}} ==High school career== Konate, who grew up playing soccer, only started playing basketball in 2014. He credits his improvement to time spent in the weight room.{{cite magazine|last1=Feldman|first1=Bruce|title=The Art of Shot Blocking: How WVU's Sagaba Konate Became a Master of Rejection|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2018/03/19/sagaba-konate-west-virginia-shot-blocker-march-madness|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|accessdate=March 23, 2018|date=March 19, 2018}} Jeff Kollar and his wife became Konate's legal guardians as he attended [[Kennedy Catholic High School (Hermitage, Pennsylvania)|Kennedy Catholic High School]].{{cite web |last1=White |first1=Mike |title=Kennedy Catholic basketball team is talented — and controversial |url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/high-school-basketball/2018/08/01/oscar-tshiebwe-recruiting-2019-class-west-virginia-kentucky-kennedy-catholic-pitt-basketball/stories/201808010157 |website=[[Pittsburgh Post-Gazette]] |accessdate=10 July 2019 |date=22 December 2017}} At the high school level, Konate earned Player of the Year and All-State honors in [[Pennsylvania]] and was a three-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] entering college.{{cite web|last1=Pellegrini|first1=Vince|title=Kennedy Catholic's Konate picks West Virginia|url=http://wkbn.com/2015/10/01/kennedy-catholics-konate-picks-west-virginia/|publisher=[[WKBN-TV]]|accessdate=March 23, 2018|date=October 1, 2015|archive-date=March 24, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180324041253/http://wkbn.com/2015/10/01/kennedy-catholics-konate-picks-west-virginia/|url-status=dead}} ==College career== As a college player, Konate established himself as an expert shot-blocker, averaging 3.2 blocks per game in his sophomore year,{{cite web|title=Sagaba Konate|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/sagaba-konate-1.html|website=Sports Reference|accessdate=May 23, 2018}} which was 3rd in the nation for Division I.{{cite web|title=NCAA Division I Men's Basketball Player Blocks Statistics - 2017-18|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/statistics/player/_/stat/blocks/year/2018/seasontype/2/group/50|website=ESPN|accessdate=May 23, 2018}} In addition, he averaged 10.8 points and 7.6 rebounds per contest. Konate flirted with the [[2018 NBA draft]], but ultimately withdrew his name and returned to West Virginia.{{cite news|last1=Norlander|first1=Matt|title=Mesmerizing shot-blocker Sagaba Konate withdraws from the NBA Draft to return to West Virginia|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/mesmerizing-shot-blocker-sagaba-konate-withdraws-from-the-nba-draft-to-return-to-west-virginia/|accessdate=May 25, 2018|work=[[CBS Sports]]|date=May 24, 2018}} During his junior year, Konate broke the WVU all-time record for blocked shots with 191. He spent most of the season sidelined due to a knee injury. After the 2018–2019 season, Konate declared for the [[2019 NBA draft]], forgoing his senior year.{{cite news |last1=Farrell |first1=Nick |title=What the new NBA Draft rules mean for Sagaba Konate, WVU |url=https://www.wvillustrated.com/wvu-basketball/what-the-new-nba-draft-rules-mean-for-sagaba-konate-wvu/ |accessdate=November 18, 2019 |work=West Virginia Illustrated |date=April 22, 2019 |archive-date=December 19, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191219203915/https://www.wvillustrated.com/wvu-basketball/what-the-new-nba-draft-rules-mean-for-sagaba-konate-wvu/ |url-status=dead }} ==Professional career== After going undrafted, Konate signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] on July 23, 2019.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/press-release/raptors-sign-robinson-brissett-konate|title=Raptors Sign Robinson, Brissett and Konate|date=July 23, 2019|work=NBA.com press release|access-date=July 23, 2019}} He was waived and then added to the roster of their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Raptors 905]].{{cite news |last1=Howe |first1=Joshua |title=Canadians Ennis, Brissett highlight Raptors 905 opening day roster |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/canadians-ennis-brissett-highlight-raptors-905-opening-day-roster/ |accessdate=November 18, 2019 |work=Sportsnet.ca |date=November 5, 2019}} Konate fractured his metatarsal in the preseason but returned in January 2020.{{cite news |last1=O'Brien |first1=Kelsea |title=Healthy 905 No Match For Agua Caliente Clippers |url=https://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2020/01/02/healthy-905-no-match-for-agua-caliente-clippers/ |accessdate=January 13, 2020 |work=Raptors Republic |date=January 2, 2020}} He averaged 4.7 points and 2.2 rebounds per game. On August 20, 2020, Konate signed with [[Basket Zaragoza|Casademont Zaragoza]] of the [[Liga ACB]].{{cite news |title=Casademont Zaragoza inks Sagaba Konate |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/casademont-zaragoza-inks-sagaba-konate/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=August 20, 2020 |date=August 20, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} On November 29, 2020, Konate announced he had signed with Greek club [[P.A.O.K. BC|PAOK Thessaloniki]]. On June 25, 2021, he signed with [[Pallacanestro Trieste]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/sagaba-konate-signs-with-trieste/|title=Sagaba Konate signs with Trieste|last=|first=|date=June 25, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=June 25, 2021|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }} On July 23, 2022, he has signed with [[ratiopharm Ulm]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/sagaba-konate-signs-2-year-deal-with-ratiopharm-ulm/|title=Sagaba Konate signs 2-year deal with Ratiopharm Ulm|last=|first=|date=July 23, 2022|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 7, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }} On July 21, 2023, he signed with [[Samsunspor Basketbol|Samsunspor]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=SSBasketbol |number=1682414375758331907 |title=Welcome Sagaba Konate!}} On August 16, 2025, he signed with [[Bursaspor Basketbol]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite tweet |user=BsBasketbol |number=1956736783720300545 |title=Hoş Geldin Sagaba Konate}} On September 4, 2025, the club announced that it had mutually parted ways with Sagaba Konate due to personal reasons.{{Cite tweet |user=BsBasketbol |number=1963601395753394280 |title=Kamuoyuna duyuru}} January 2, 2026, Sagaba Konate joined [[Zastal Zielona Góra]]. He has a contract valid until the end of the 2025/2026 season.{{Cite web |title=Sagaba Konate nowym Zastalowcem! |url=https://basketzg.pl/posts/sagaba-konate-nowym-zastalowcem/954
